text.content: The installation locations are all spaces that the urban life passes through: outside of buildings, sometimes the insides, walls, the pavement, abudments… These, the cities indeed, are spaces that these animals would normally not exist, nor would they ever want to. One can’t think of a rhino or a moose to calmly just pass through Kadife Street, or a bear quietly strolling down the Yüksek Kaldırım staircase in broad daylight. There are just a few species that have managed to adapt to the city habitat, cats, dogs, some birds, insects and bacteria. There isn’t much chance we could encounter any other creature anyways. We would not let them.

text.content: “The cities come into being independently of the rhythms of nature. They treat nature and natural life as a mere commodity in it’s coming into being. Sand is a singularized item that is to be converted into glass; marble is something only if it is a column or a gravestone; a wooden staircase; an elevator or like window blinds… Hence nature can exist only as a utility or a decoration, as a side to the main constructed being that is the city. A tree in a rectangular pot on wheels exists on the rooftop only to be rolled around to provide us shade as we pick where we want to be.”

text.content: It took me nearly four years to capture the frames in this film. From beginning to end, in less than a minute, an entire lifetime passes before our eyes. text.content: A dreamy psychedelic pop track inspired by a flamingo and rhinoceros walking side by side under a surreal moonlight. The music should feature a slow, flowing groove with layered synth textures, blending warm analog bass lines with soft, high-pitched melodic elements (like toy piano, glockenspiel, or ambient guitar swells). Each creature is represented sonically: the flamingo with fluttery, melodic arpeggios; the rhino with grounded, distorted pads and earthy percussion. Include reverb-drenched ambient elements to evoke an otherworldly, lunar landscape. Vocals should be soft, almost whispered—perhaps a duet or overlapping harmonies—carrying abstract lyrics about unlikely companionship and quiet journeys. The tone is surreal, gentle, and slightly emotional—like two misfits walking in rhythm, unbothered by the world’s logic.

text.content: "Distopik bir kabustan gelen dark-jazz ve avant-garde bir kompozisyon. Saldırgan saksafon riff’leri, boğuk yaylıların ve kırık, sert davulların üzerine binerek huzursuz bir ritim oluşturuyor. Enstrümanlar, sanki bir tartışma içindeymiş gibi çarpışıyor ve yankılanıyor, gerginlik ile boşluk arasında gidip gelen bir dans yaratıyor. Sesler bazen birbirine dolanıyor, bazen de aniden susarak kesik bir sessizlik bırakıyor. Dissonant akorlar ve beklenmedik tempo değişimleri, korku ve içgüdülerin çatışmasını yansıtıyor. Elektronik dokunuşlar ve geriye sarılmış ses örnekleri, gerçeklik algısını kırarak müziğe halüsinatif bir hava katıyor."

text.content: "A chaotic, suffocating dark-jazz piece. Dissonant saxophones, clashing drums, and murky strings convulse within a fragmented rhythm, oscillating between noise and silence, creating an ever-growing tension."

text.content: "A dystopian nightmare embodied in dark jazz and avant-garde composition. Aggressive saxophone riffs intertwine with murky strings and fractured, sharp drums, forming an unsettling rhythm. Instruments crash and echo as if engaged in an argument, creating a dance between tension and void. Sounds tangle together, then suddenly vanish into abrupt silence. Dissonant chords and unpredictable tempo shifts mirror the clash of fear and instinct. Electronic elements and reversed sound samples distort the perception of reality, adding a hallucinatory atmosphere to the composition."

text.content: Create an neo classic, avant-garde experimental sound art composition driven entirely by vocalizations of a single dog, Classic organ and fulute. The piece should use a wide range of canine vocal expressions including deep barks, high-pitched yelps, growls, howls, whimpers, snorts, and rhythmic panting. Structure the vocals rhythmically like percussive elements, using looped barks as beats and howls as melodic drones. Incorporate glitchy textures, industrial noise elements, and ambient dark pads to create a tense yet absurd atmosphere. The composition should feel like a theatrical monologue from a dog trying to communicate in a human-dominated urban environment. Imagine the dog as the narrator of the city’s chaos — not through words, but through the language of sound, tension, and instinct.

text.content: A surreal and emotive art-pop composition inspired by a faceless child figure embracing a luminous, alien-like octopus in a textured, dreamlike space. The music should blend soft, childlike melodies (music box tones, plucked toy piano, light glockenspiel) with experimental textures—glitchy tape noise, reversed elements, and ambient pads that mimic the blurry subconscious. Vocals should be ethereal, whispery, wordless or fragmented, resembling distant memories or imagined lullabies. Harmonies can be strange but gentle—dissonant at times, but never harsh. Include warm bass pulses and subtle, heartbeat-like percussion to reflect the quiet tension between affection and ambiguity. The mood is intimate, magical, and emotionally complex—like a dream you almost remember but can’t explain.

The music should feature spacious reverb-heavy textures, slow analog pads, layered organic synths, and gentle melodic fragments—like fading memories. The elephant is expressed through deep, earthy drones and warm low-end pulses; the seahorse through soft, twinkling tones (music box, glassy keys, glockenspiel, reversed melodies). Include breathy, wordless harmonies or occasional whispered vocal textures to suggest presence without narrative. The rhythm is nearly absent—more of a pulse than a beat. The tone should feel sacred, soft, cosmic, and timeless—like a lullaby written by gravity itself.

text.content: The object and its essence; a concept and its essence; and finally: the image of this essence. The spirit of a face, or the face of a concept. How would a concept gaze at us and how would we see it? Does the forest spirit look like a deer? What kind of images would we face if we were to try to capture the essence of things? Could a sensation such as “Curiosity” —or even “Fire” as something we assume to know how to physically represent so well— obtain a spirit and how does this materialize in our physical actuality? How does it look at us from its conceptual realm gazing into the physical? What other sensation arises when curiosity is personified? Does the image of an emotion or of a concept look like the concept itself?

text.content: So as I was searching for the answers to these questions, I found myself mixing paint and making concoctions on paper. The works I present to you are the products of this ritualistic study.

text.content: These rituals are made as monoprints as the first paint markings are transferred onto the next frames before it sets, and fades one by one through each frame. And it is followed by the second paint layer and, one by one is transferred across every frame and every round, as it fades until disappearing. The third layer, then the fourth, maybe a smear here, a stroke there… The cycle repeats itself until the face obtains a gaze. I'm just painting the first frame. Others are just reflections of the first frame.  The spirit emerges.

Çevre dostu materyal:  WWF Market’te bulacağınız ürünlerde çevre dostu ve adil üretim şartları gözetilir ve tüm süreçlerde sürdürülebilir yöntemler ön plandadır. Bu koleksiyonda bulacağınız t-shirt ve çantaların üretiminde çevreye saygılı biçimde üretilmiş  %100 GOTS sertifikalı organik Ege pamuğu  tercih edildi. Kumaşların bir kısmında ise organik pamukla beraber kumaşın mukavemetini ve ömrünü artıran, geri dönüştürülmüş PES ipliği ile örülmüş  GRS    (Global Recycle Standard)    sertifikalı  materyaller kullanıldı.      WWF Market:  Dünya genelinde karşı karşıya olduğumuz iklim değişikliği, küresel ısınma gibi insan kaynaklı problemler, doğa ve doğa hayatını tehdit ediyor. Buna dair çalışmalarını sürdüren  WWF Türkiye (Doğal Hayatı Koruma Vakfı)  ve tekstil odaklı tasarım ve üretim ofisi   Reflect Studio   iş birliğinde yürütülen WWF Market, canlı türlerini ve yaşam alanlarını korumayı hedefleyen çalışmalara destek olabileceğiniz ürünlere ulaşmanızı sağlıyor. WWF Market x Kaybid koleksiyonuna buradan ulaşabilir,  wwfmarket.com  web sitesinden de WWF Market’teki tüm ürünleri inceleyebilirsiniz.     Kaybid:  Çalışmalarında nesli tükenmekte ve tehdit altında olan hayvanları, onların yabancı olduğu kentsel ekosisteme taşıyan ve izleyene dünyanın sadece insanlara ait olmadığını hatırlatmayı amaçlayan Kaybid’in işleri, bu sefer de WWF Market ürünleri üzerinde harekete geçiyor. Çalışmalarını farklı mecralarda yürüten sanatçının işlerini daha detaylı incelemek isterseniz; Kaybid’in  web sitesini  ve  Instagram hesabını  inceleyebilir veya İstanbul’un kuytu köşelerindeki duvarlarda bu hayvanları takibe çıkabilirsiniz.     Aposto! okurlarına özel  48 saatlik  %20 indirimden  faydalanmak için, 25 Temmuz 23.59’a kadar geçerli  aposto20  indirim kodunu  kullanabilirsiniz.

link_mention.title: MIXER'in Yeni Sergisi "Printed '20" Kapılarını Açtı
link_mention.description: MIXER‘in ilki 2015 yılında hayata geçirilen ve baskı sanatına odaklanan sergi serisi “PRINTED”ın 6. edisyonu “Printed ’20” hafta sonunda kapılarını açtı. Serginin küratörlüğü x-ist’in kurucu ortağı ve The Empire Project’in kurucusu ve yöneticisi Kerimcan Güleryüz üstlenirken, sergi seçkisi usta sanatçılar ile genç kuşağın dikkat çeken isimlerini bir araya getiriyor.  Sergide işleri izleyiciyle buluşan sanatçılar ise Burhan Kum, CANAN, Erol Akyavaş, Edze Ali, Jordan Söderberg Mills, Kaybid, Lale Tara, Mehmet Güleryüz, SENA, Stoya, Ünal Baş ve Yekateryna Grygorenko. “Printed ’20” gravürden linolyum baskıya, heykelden fotoğrafa farklı nesiller ve medyumlarda üretim yapan sanatçıların baskı ve çoğaltılabilir eserlerinin dönemsel olarak değişimlerini izleme olanağı sunuyor.
